author: Chris Pinson
title: Bears lose conference opener to Hilltoppers - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Pinson ,
1 hours ago
BOWLING GREEN, KY--The Missouri State football team suffered a 21-point loss to Western Kentucky in its Conference USA opener, Thursday night.
The Bears (1-4, 0-1) fell, 34-13 to the Hilltoppers (2-4, 1-0) on the road. It was the second year in-a-row WKU defeated MSU. However, this was the 10th consecutive meeting the Hilltoppers got the best of the Bears.
Missouri State turned the ball over twice and managed to kick just two field goals in the first half, while Western Kentucky scored three touchdowns -- two coming off MO State's turnovers -- to lead 21-6 at the half.
Early in the 3rd quarter, Bears starting quarterback, Skylar Locklear, got injured running for a first down. Locklear ran into a pair of Hilltoppers defenders and limped off the field, which allowed backup Henry Belin IV the chance to try and give the offense a spark.
Belin made the most of that opportunity and drove MSU down the field, and threw a 36-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Meyers to cut the deficit to 21-13.
However, that would be the last score of the night for MSU. They only got three more possessions after that, and had to punt, then turned the ball over on downs their final two drives.
The Hilltoppers would add a couple field goals to their total and seal the game with a 39-yard touchdown run to secure the victory.
Bears Head Coach Casey Woods will address the media on Friday, so it'll be interesting to hear his thoughts on if he has a quarterback competition on his hands now.
